papers.summary: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $Δ$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongrácz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongrácz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $Γ$ of $Δ$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $Γ$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $Γ$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.sence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, i.e., a purely algebraic condition.
papers.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms

papers.summary: This paper presents a novel fourth-order, L-stable exponential time differencing (ETD) Runge-Kutta type scheme incorporating a dimensional splitting integrating factor method for the numerical solution of nonlinear reaction-diffusion systems. The method, ETDRK4RDP-IF, is obtained by approximating the matrix exponential operators in the classical dimensionally split ETDRK-IF scheme with an accurate fourth-order, L-acceptable rational function with real and distinct poles. The L-acceptability of the rational approximation guarantees effective damping of spurious oscillations arising from nonsmooth initial and/or boundary data and further eliminates complex arithmetic in the solution of the associated linear systems, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and making the scheme well-suited for parallel implementation in low-level programming languages such as Fortran and C++. Numerical experiments confirm the fourth-order accuracy for a range of reaction-diffusion problems with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and demonstrate that it outperforms existing standard ETD methods in serial and parallel implementations, yielding CPU time reductions of up to a factor of 20.
papers.title: A fourth-order dimensionally split exponential time differencing scheme with real and distinct pole rational approximation for non-linear reaction-diffusion systems

papers.summary: We generalize the notion of an independent family on $ω$ to $\mathcal{J}$-independent families on an arbitrary cardinal $κ$ and then show that under determinacy-like hypotheses that there can be no such families for reasonable $\mathcal{J}$. This is quite atypical as all other generalizations of the kinds of combinatorial families coming from the theory of cardinal characteristics follow a very different pattern, which will also be explained; in this sense independent families seem particularly special. The base theory assumed throughout is $\textsf{ZF + }$All infinite sets are Dedekind infinite.
papers.title: Independent Families Under Determinacy-Like Hypotheses

papers.summary: For nonlocal interface evolution problems such as the Mullins-Sekerka flow, certain parametric schemes discretize only the interface and approximate the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map by boundary elements. Their error analysis requires bounds on how this discrete operator changes as the polygon moves. In that analysis, the polygons are only Lipschitz and close to a smooth curve only in a Lipschitz norm, the perturbations are controlled only in the energy norm, and the kernels are singular on the diagonal. We study the symmetric Galerkin boundary element matrix on the polygons in a Lipschitz neighborhood of a smooth reference curve. Its first variation, tested against discrete Neumann solutions, is bounded by the energy norm of the perturbation alone. The second-order remainder of the associated mass form is bounded by the product of the energy norm and the Lipschitz norm of the perturbation, so that only one of the two factors needs a uniform bound. On the interpolating polygon, the matrix is consistent with the continuous operator without the logarithmic loss that a pointwise comparison of the kernels would suggest, and its shape derivative is consistent with that of the continuous operator. All bounds are uniform in the mesh size and depend only on the constants of the reference curve.
papers.title: Shape Perturbation of the Galerkin Boundary Element Dirichlet-to-Neumann Matrix on Moving Polygons

papers.summary: This paper studies the numerical approximation of a mathematical model of coupled flow and viscoelastic deformation in a fractured porous medium including fracture contact mechanics. We consider a mixed-dimensional model, where the fracture is modeled as a co-dimension one object within the porous medium. This model couples Darcy flow in the matrix and fracture, linear viscoelasticity of the matrix and frictional contact mechanics of the fracture surfaces; the contact conditions include normal compliance and a Coulomb friction law. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.
papers.title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium

papers.summary: The convection-diffusion problem has been studied extensively as an important model for convection-dominated problems. The problem becomes more challenging when the convecting velocity is no longer Lipschitz and merely has Sobolev regularity. In this paper, we use Boyer's extension of the DiPerna--Lions theory for the transport equation to study the vanishing diffusion limit of discretizations of the convection-diffusion equation with Sobolev velocity. In the case of flux-adapted boundary conditions, we prove that a continuous Galerkin discretization converges strongly to the renormalized solution of the transport equation as the diffusion coefficient and mesh size go to zero, without requiring any relationship between them. We refer to this unconditional strong convergence as asymptotic robustness. In the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions, we use the renormalization theory and barrier arguments to prove that a piecewise constant hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin scheme is asymptotically robust, while the continuous Galerkin scheme may fail to converge. Our results indicate that the asymptotic robustness of schemes for the convection-diffusion problem depends on the realization of the boundary conditions as opposed to internal layers.
papers.title: Asymptotic Robustness of HDG Schemes for the Convection-Diffusion Equation

papers.summary: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $μ$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $μ(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrectifiable measures with any prescribed exact Hausdorff and packing dimensions $0\leq s_H\leq s_P\leq q$ with $m-1\leq s_P\leq m$, which are doubling when $s_H>0$. This verifies a conjecture of Badger and Schul. The design of the measures relies on metric cubes with variable scaling, in which the ratio of consecutive side lengths tends to infinity but jumps only on a sparse set of generations, together with Badger and Schul's square packing construction of Lipschitz maps.
papers.title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions

papers.summary: The well-known Wu--Zhang question asks whether every Noetherian Hopf algebra over a field is affine (finitely generated as an algebra). In this paper, we extend this fundamental problem to the braided setting within the monoidal category ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ of left Yetter--Drinfel'd modules over a Hopf algebra $H$. By developing term-rewriting methods based on reduction orderings and prime-word factorizations in free prebraided algebras, we establish explicit expansions for YD-triangular comultiplications. We prove that if $(\mathbb{K}\langle X \rangle, ε)$ is an augmented free algebra in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ and $I \subseteq \ker ε$ is an ideal invariant under a YD-triangular comultiplication, then every $I$-reducible letter---and consequently every non-empty word in $\langle X \rangle$---can be expressed modulo $I$ as a linear combination of products of $I$-irreducible letters strictly smaller with respect to the reduction order. As a primary consequence, we prove that any right Noetherian connected prebraided Hopf algebra $B$ in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ is affine, generated by the image of a finite set $X_{I}$ of $I$-irreducible letters. As an application, we show that the braided component $B = A^{\mathrm{co}\,π}$ of a right Noetherian Radford biproduct $A = B \sharp H$ is affine whenever $A_{(0)} \subseteq \jmath(H)$, reducing the affineness of $A$ entirely to that of $H$.
papers.title: Noetherian connected braided Hopf algebras are affine

papers.summary: While scattering resonances of plane-embedded cavities have wide-ranging engineering applications, numerical results for such configurations remain virtually unexplored. We present an effective finite element approach for computing these resonances. The unbounded domain is truncated using a Dirichlet-to-Neumann(DtN) boundary operator, recasting the problem as the eigenvalue problem of a holomorphic Fredholm operator function. Discretization is carried out using Lagrange finite elements with a truncated DtN expansion, and convergence is rigorously proven using Karma's approximation theory. The resulting non-linear matrix eigenvalue system is computed using a multi-step parallel spectral indicator method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical predictions and provide benchmark solutions for future investigations.
papers.title: Scattering Resonances of Plane-Embedded Cavities: A Finite Element DtN Approach

papers.summary: A new notion of a coz-included sublocale is introduced. It is a necessary condition for a sublocale to be a dense $C$-embedding, and together with the property of being well-embedded, is sufficient. However, although it is clearly a strengthening of coz-ontoness (or z-embeddings), it is incomparable with $C^*$-embeddings as is demonstrated by the Čech-Stone compactification of the real numbers. Motivated by non-trivial spatial examples, this new notion and other weaker variants, such as casi coz-included and relative zero sublocales, are explored and characterized in the point-free setting. As a consequence, new characterizations of several classes of frames, such as perfectly normal and $Oz$ frames, among others, are provided. Besides the lattice theoretic interpretations, there are some interesting topological ramifications.
papers.title: The Čech-Stone compactification of the reals and coz-included sublocales

papers.summary: Let $γ$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_γ$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,δ)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$.
papers.title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure

papers.summary: We consider a subclass of the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ weights with added smoothness, which we refer to as flattening weights $F_2.$ We quantify how such weights arise as exponents of VMO functions and prove that monotone rearrangement does not increase the class modulus in $F_2.$
papers.title: Monotone Rearrangement for Flattening Weights $F_2$

papers.summary: Let $A$ be a Nakayama algebra and $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ its stable Auslander algebra. We introduce a new homological invariant, called the finitistic Gorenstein dimension, which coincides with the classical Gorenstein dimension whenever the latter is finite, and compute this invariant for $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ when $A$ has infinite global dimension. Combined with an accompanying criterion for the finiteness of the Gorenstein dimension of $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$, our results provide a complete description of this dimension and verify the Gorenstein Symmetry Conjecture for this class of algebras. Furthermore, we show that the finitistic Gorenstein dimension of $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $ is also left-right symmetric, is explicitly related to the finitistic dimension of $A$, and can be attained among the injective dimensions of the projective $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $-modules corresponding to simple $A$-modules. Our proofs rely on computing injective dimensions in terms of distances in the coresolution forest of $A$, a combinatorial structure closely related to Ringel's coresolution quiver.
papers.title: Gorenstein dimensions for stable Auslander algebras of Nakayama algebras

papers.summary: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. This resolves the Erdős similarity problem in the large.
papers.title: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large

papers.summary: In this paper, we study Goncharov-type Rota-Baxter operators in the framework of group-graded Hopf pi-algebras. By constructing convolution pi-algebras as the core calculus tool, we systematically derive fundamental algebraic properties of Hopf pi-algebras, including antipode anti-homomorphism and generalized homomorphism compatibility. On this basis, we establish the axiomatic system of two classes of graded Rota-Baxter operators of weight 1 and weight -1, prove their bijective correspondence via the antipode, construct several non-trivial examples, and present two derived structures: descendant Hopf pi-algebras and image Hopf pi-subalgebras. This work enriches the operator theory of graded Hopf algebras and provides algebraic constructions for related research on graded Yang-Baxter equations.
papers.title: From convolution pi-algebras to Rota-Baxter Hopf pi-algebras

papers.summary: In this paper, we extend the technique of Lerner, Ombrosi and Rivera-Ríos (Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 51(1): 107--119, 2019) for the necessity of the strong-type boundedness of commutators to the endpoint case, and give characterizations of BMO via the endpoint bounds for commutators of singular integrals with rough kernels and related operators, which improve the conditions of Accomazzo (Israel J. Math. 228(2): 787--800, 2018), Guo et al. (J. Geom. Anal. 30(4): 3995-4035, 2020). We also give a characterization of BMO via the endpoint bounds for commutators of non-degenerate Calderón-Zygmund operators by removing the real-valued restriction on pointwise multiplier, which extend the results of Hytönen (J. Math. Pures Appl. (9) 156: 351--391, 2021) to the endpoint case. Finally, we find counterexamples to illustrate that weighted endpoint estimate of commutator of fractional integral operator does not necessarily imply $b\in{\rm BMO}$, and two-weighted endpoint estimate of Bloom type for commutator of Hilbert transform does not hold, which are missing for a long time.
papers.title: Improvement to characterizations of BMO in terms of endpoint bounds for commutators and some counterexamples

papers.summary: Inspired by recent work of A. Njamcul and A. Pavlović, we study topological spaces expanded by ideals of sets. We investigate the relationship between the cardinal invariants of the ideal topological space $(X, τ_\mathcal{I})$, the underlying topology $(X, τ)$, and the cardinal characteristics of the ideal $\mathcal{I}$. Furthermore, we analyze continuous maps between standard Polish spaces and their ideal expansions. We establish rigidity phenomena showing that continuous functions from $(X, τ)$ into $(X, τ_\mathcal{I})$ are severely constrained (e.g., taking at most countably many values on Polish spaces and being strictly constant on $\mathbb{R}$), whereas continuous functions from $(\mathbb{R}, τ_\mathcal{I})$ to $(\mathbb{R}, τ)$ collapse to standard continuous functions under mild conditions on the ideal.
papers.title: Topology idealized

papers.summary: Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic in which every term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation. RGA discharges a hypothesis only when it proves the hypothesis decided. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, how Gödel's incompleteness theorems hold for RGA and for systems built on it. RGA's implication is material and RGA has the disjunction property, so the implications the textbook proof of the second theorem uses fail while its entailments and rules hold: Gödel's proof survives as entailments. RGA does not prove its consistency sentence Con, and RGA derives its own second theorem as the entailment $\mathit{Con}\vdash\neg\mathit{Pr}(\ulcorner\mathit{Con}\urcorner)$ and as one sentence quantified over proofs. The second theorem is then proved once, for every Gödel extension of RGA: an entailment relation on RGA's language, closed under RGA's rules, with a checker that meets three structural conditions, NEC, D3 and EXPL as proof transformers, D1 as closed acceptance, and consistency. D2 is not among the conditions. RGA with its checker is one instance. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA), RGA with ground induction, is another, its checker adding one rule detector, and IGA does not derive its consistency sentence for it. Adoption, a reflection rule whose premise is a derived warrant that the checker accepts computed proofs of every instance of a universal, gives consistent extensions RGA$^+$ and IGA$^+$. RGA$^+$ derives RGA's consistency sentence and IGA$^+$ derives RGA's and IGA's, so each strictly extends its base, and IGA$^+$ both. The second theorem holds at every adopted notation claim, and adopting Turing's code for that claim's checker derives its consistency sentence, so no claim certifies itself. Whether IGA alone derives RGA's consistency sentence is open, and the paper names what two routes to an answer need.
papers.title: Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems in Grounded Arithmetic

papers.summary: For any given uncountable cardinal $κ$, we show that every $κ$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_κ\star1$ (the $κ$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $κ$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $κ$.
papers.title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
